capabilities.reason: Athena applies Lake Formation fine-grained filtering (column-level, row-level) only on engine version 3; engines v1/v2 fall back to coarse IAM/table-level access.
limitations: Engine v3 must be selected on the workgroup.
Querying a governed table with insufficient LF permissions fails the query rather than silently filtering.

capabilities.reason: Glue 5.0 added native Lake Formation fine-grained access control for Spark jobs; earlier versions enforce LF only for catalog resolution and governed-table writes.
limitations: Glue <5.0 reads data via the job role's IAM/S3 permissions, not per-principal LF grants, unless the job uses the LF integration path.
Glue 5.0 FGAC requires the job to run under an LF-registered access model.

capabilities.reason: EMR on EC2 integrates with Lake Formation for Spark/EMRFS access from release 5.32, but only when a security configuration with the LF integration is attached.
limitations: Requires a security configuration enabling Lake Formation and an IAM role for the integration.
Hive and Presto on EMR have different LF support matrices than Spark.

capabilities.reason: Filtered (partial) access to governed tables is only possible through engine v3 with row/column filters defined via data cells filters; whole-table DENY semantics are unchanged.
limitations: Row filters require an aws_lakeformation_data_cells_filter referenced by a grant.

capabilities.reason: Glue reads on governed tables honor data-cells filters only on the LF-integrated path (Glue 5.0 native FGAC or governed-table jobs); plain DynamicFrame reads bypass filters.
limitations: Jobs reading via IAM on unregistered S3 paths bypass LF entirely.

capabilities.reason: Hybrid access mode lets a data location serve both IAM-governed and LF-governed principals while workloads migrate; it is a registration/catalog setting, not a versioned engine feature.
limitations: With IAMAllowedPrincipals defaults retained, new tables are IAM-governed unless explicitly enrolled.
Effective access under hybrid mode is the union of IAM and LF evaluation - over-broad defaults defeat LF filtering.

capabilities.reason: Cross-account LF grants require an AWS RAM resource share and, for LF-tag-based sharing across accounts, CROSS_ACCOUNT_VERSION 3 in the catalog settings.
limitations: Named-resource cross-account grants work at version 1+; LF-TBAC across accounts requires version 3.
The consumer must create a resource link before local principals can query.
